cells.tense: You are here with the pen, holding what needs to end before you speak a word of it.
cells.act: decide it and act the same day, without explaining
cells.ask: Take the ending that has settled under everything you haven't said. Decide it, and do the one next thing today — no explaining first, no waiting for better phrasing.
cells.core:
You can stand where something has finished and read what belongs to the part that just ended. The weighing happens before speech, and it comes out accurate. In the middle of that, you can decide something and do the next thing while the day is still the same day, and the decision carries because it only had to move one step.

So the next ending sitting there, decided under everything you haven't said yet — don't spend the week finding its sentence. Decide it and do the next thing now. The clearing only shows itself after the door is shut; until then the closing stays private, which is exactly where it keeps costing you something.

cells.tense: The ending is going to happen, so every word of it is being written ahead of time.
cells.act: go on toward it without needing a sign
cells.ask: Continue with what you chose after the ending — no sign it's working, no check on whether to keep going, for as long as you said you would.
cells.core:
You can feel the ending approaching, so you start living on the far side of it — drafting the conversation, planning the aftermath, bracing for how it will land. The weighing that usually keeps you clear has run ahead of events. The place you are in is still here and half of you has already moved out.

Thinking it through harder won't end the bracing. Go on toward what you chose after the ending — with nothing confirming it is working, no check-in, and the doubt permitted. The step is smaller than the bracing and does not need the ending solved first. Continuing without a sign is what you did once before; the next step is that same act, done again.

cells.tense: You have been held at a door that closed on its own, still working out the right words for it.
cells.act: savour the realised thing without reaching past it
cells.ask: Something finished and doesn't need you now. Stay with what it gave you, whole as it is, and reach past it toward nothing yet.
cells.core:
There is a door behind you that has already closed, and you are held there, wording what happened. The cleared space ahead of you hasn't been entered. The reading that usually arrives to you early is stalled on old material, and nothing has landed here yet.

Pushing forward will not fix this; it only makes the cleared space louder. Stay with one thing that genuinely finished — enjoying what it gave you, reaching toward nothing past it, telling no one. What has drained away returns quietly when a finished thing is allowed to be finished. Let one satisfaction land, and the closed door stops being the only place you can stand.

cells.tense: You are already clearing the room for other people while describing it as the way things simply are.
cells.act: let the exchange with someone run both ways
cells.ask: Say what you see finishing in someone's life — plainly, once — then let their answer change what you do next, without you shaping it.
cells.core:
You can tell when something in another person's life has finished, and you begin clearing it for them — the shortened conversation, the plan already adjusted, the version of the ending you hold so it lands gently. You experience this as noticing rather than steering. Whoever is living next door is living in a room you prepared without saying so.

That preparation belongs on the table where it can be answered. Say what you see finishing in someone's life, plainly, once — and let their answer change what you do next. What you have been handing over unnamed is the exact thing the exchange has been missing, and giving it your name is all the next move requires.

attempts.check: The unsupported claim is that the person withholds knowing until the right moment, which the record cannot confirm as a practice rather than a temperament. A reader could reasonably object that they are not deciding anything, they are simply unsure, and the card is reading selection where there is fog. The asks survive that: each names one small act of deciding and acting anyway, useful whether the pause is chosen or frightened. The sentence that serves the writer more than the person is any line implying the pause is deliberate strength, so the cells should leave the pause unjudged and put the weight on what gets closed.
